OpenCode Plugins Not Loading? Check V1, V2 and Plugin Scope

Run opencode --version on the machine loading the plugin. Then check whether the missing feature runs on the server, in Desktop, or in the terminal. A V1 plugin needs a V2 implementation to run on V2; changing the config key alone cannot fix it.

  1. Check a missing server plugin
  2. Check a missing Desktop panel or terminal command
  3. Check whether the plugin targets V1 or V2
  4. Reproduce a server load with a local marker
  5. Sources and related checks

Where is your OpenCode plugin missing?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Check a missing server plugin

  1. Run opencode --version on the machine running the server. If you are attached to a remote server, changes to your local project config may not reach it.
  2. Keep a backup of your configuration before editing. For V2, put the maintainer’s exact package specifier in the plugins array in opencode.json(c). For a local plugin, use a directory path relative to that config file, or put it under .opencode/plugins/ for discovery. A configured single-file path is skipped in V2. Use only packages you trust: a plugin runs code in OpenCode.
  3. Look for matching disable entries in all active V2 configs. The arrays combine, and a later rule can disable a plugin. For a global package install, opencode plugin list helps confirm the entry; then check the plugin’s own expected server feature in a fresh session. A listed package alone does not prove its server feature works.

If a trusted package is still missing, check for a package or load error before changing more settings. V2 can install missing packages after startup; check again once installation finishes. Keep startup logs local unless you have reviewed them for credentials and private paths.

Check a missing Desktop panel or terminal command

In V2, check what the package actually exports. A server-only plugin has no Desktop panel or terminal UI. For Desktop, check that the package has a GUI part, put it in the global config for the app’s own server, and check Settings → Extensions → Plugins. Its switch controls the Desktop UI; it does not turn off the server part. If it shows a UI load failure, use Reload and confirm the intended panel or command appears.

A terminal-only package belongs in the terminal client’s cli.json, under plugins. A package with both server and terminal parts can be configured on the server; check the package’s instructions for your client. Verify the named command or panel in the client where the package says it appears.

Check whether the plugin targets V1 or V2

Match the installed major version to the maintainer’s supported release. V1 uses plugin for package entries; native V2 uses plugins. V2 can read supported legacy configuration, but V1 plugin implementations need to be ported to the new API. A renamed setting or relocated file will not port the implementation.

If you cannot determine the generation, start from the version command, check the package release notes, and test only a known compatible version in a scratch project. Before removing anything from your regular workspace, keep a copy of the configuration and change one entry at a time.

Reproduce a server load with a local marker

Use an empty scratch Git project with OpenCode 2.4.1. Create .opencode/plugins/local-probe/index.ts with this fixture:

import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "ipunk.local-probe",
  async setup() {
    writeFileSync(process.env.IPUNK_PLUGIN_MARKER, "IPUNK_LOCAL_PLUGIN_READY")
  },
})

From the scratch project, run these commands (macOS or Linux shell):

IPUNK_PLUGIN_MARKER="$PWD/plugin-ready.txt" \
  opencode debug agents --standalone --print-logs --log-level debug
cat plugin-ready.txt

Use a fresh project or delete the marker from a previous run before comparing results. Seeing IPUNK_LOCAL_PLUGIN_READY in the file confirms this fixture's setup ran. This uses a private OpenCode server for the check and needs no model request.

On macOS arm64, we compared the auto-discovered directory, an explicitly configured directory, and the same configured path pointing directly to index.ts. The first two wrote the marker when run with debug agents; the file entry was skipped with a directory warning. In these runs plugin list alone reported no plugins for all three. See the recorded results.
